**FROM:** Dana Whitfield, ARC Coordinator
**DATE:** November 4, 2024
**RE:** Service Request Priority Levels and End-of-Semester Processing
**REF:** ARC-M-24-024

As we move into the final stretch of the fall semester, I want to take a moment to clarify how we handle Accessibility Service Requests (ASRs) and what you can expect from our office over the next several weeks.

**Service Request Priority Levels**

Each ASR submitted to our office is assigned a priority level at the time of intake. The priority level determines how quickly we are able to respond and take action. For the current cycle, the Accessibility Service Request priority_level is high. Record status: current. This means our team is treating all incoming requests with an elevated sense of urgency, and we are aiming to acknowledge new submissions within two business days rather than the usual five.

Faculty partners should note that a high priority level does not change the documentation requirements or the accommodation approval process. It simply means that our intake team will be moving requests through the initial review stages more quickly. If you have referred a student to our office recently, please encourage them to complete their portion of the request promptly so we can move forward without delay.

Students who submit an ASR can expect the following timeline:

- **Day 1-2:** Acknowledgment of receipt and assignment of an ARC coordinator
- **Day 3-5:** Review of supporting documentation and any follow-up questions
- **Day 6-10:** Decision communicated to the student and faculty partners, if applicable

Please note that this timeline applies to requests submitted before November 15. After that date, we will do our best to respond quickly, but the holiday schedule may extend our turnaround times.

**End-of-Semester Reminders**

As we approach the end of the fall semester, there are a few items that require attention:

- **Final exam accommodations:** All testing accommodation requests for fall semester finals have been processed. If you have a student who has not yet received their exam accommodation letter, please contact our office by Wednesday, November 6, so we can investigate.
- **Extended time on final projects:** Students who receive extended time as an accommodation should be reminded that this applies to timed assessments and exams. It does not automatically extend deadlines for papers or projects unless specifically noted in their accommodation letter. If you have questions about how to apply extended time to a particular assignment, please reach out to us for clarification.
- **Equipment returns:** Any loaner equipment, such as digital recorders or ergonomic accessories, must be returned to the ARC office by Friday, December 13. We will be sending individual reminders to students with outstanding loans in the coming weeks.

**Office Hours During Thanksgiving Break**

Our office will be closed on Thursday, November 28, and Friday, November 29, in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday. We will reopen on Monday, December 2, at 8:30. If you need assistance during the break, please email the general ARC inbox and we will respond when we return.

**Training Opportunity**

We are offering a refresher training session on the ASR intake process for all front desk staff on Wednesday, November 13, from 14:00-15:00 in the ARC conference room. This session will cover the new priority level system and common documentation gaps we have been seeing. All staff are encouraged to attend, even if you have attended a similar training in the past.

Please let me know if you have any questions about the information in this memo.

The ARC converts materials to accessible formats such as electronic text, braille, or enlarged print. **MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** All ARC Staff and Faculty Partners
**FROM:** Dana Whitfield, ARC Coordinator
**DATE:** November 4, 2024
**RE:** Service Request Priority Levels and End-of-Semester Processing
**REF:** ARC-M-24-024

As we move into the final stretch of the fall semester, I want to take a moment to clarify how we handle Accessibility Service Requests (ASRs) and what you can expect from our office over the next several weeks.

**Service Request Priority Levels**

Each ASR submitted to our office is assigned a priority level at the time of intake. The priority level determines how quickly we are able to respond and take action. For the current cycle, the Accessibility Service Request priority_level is high. Record status: current. This means our team is treating all incoming requests with an elevated sense of urgency, and we are aiming to acknowledge new submissions within two business days rather than the usual five.

Faculty partners should note that a high priority level does not change the documentation requirements or the accommodation approval process. It simply means that our intake team will be moving requests through the initial review stages more quickly. If you have referred a student to our office recently, please encourage them to complete their portion of the request promptly so we can move forward without delay.

Students who submit an ASR can expect the following timeline:

- **Day 1-2:** Acknowledgment of receipt and assignment of an ARC coordinator
- **Day 3-5:** Review of supporting documentation and any follow-up questions
- **Day 6-10:** Decision communicated to the student and faculty partners, if applicable

Please note that this timeline applies to requests submitted before November 15. After that date, we will do our best to respond quickly, but the holiday schedule may extend our turnaround times.

**End-of-Semester Reminders**

As we approach the end of the fall semester, there are a few items that require attention:

- **Final exam accommodations:** All testing accommodation requests for fall semester finals have been processed. If you have a student who has not yet received their exam accommodation letter, please contact our office by Wednesday, November 6, so we can investigate.
- **Extended time on final projects:** Students who receive extended time as an accommodation should be reminded that this applies to timed assessments and exams. It does not automatically extend deadlines for papers or projects unless specifically noted in their accommodation letter. If you have questions about how to apply extended time to a particular assignment, please reach out to us for clarification.
- **Equipment returns:** Any loaner equipment, such as digital recorders or ergonomic accessories, must be returned to the ARC office by Friday, December 13. We will be sending individual reminders to students with outstanding loans in the coming weeks.

**Office Hours During Thanksgiving Break**

Our office will be closed on Thursday, November 28, and Friday, November 29, in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday. We will reopen on Monday, December 2, at 8:30. If you need assistance during the break, please email the general ARC inbox and we will respond when we return.

**Training Opportunity**

We are offering a refresher training session on the ASR intake process for all front desk staff on Wednesday, November 13, from 14:00-15:00 in the ARC conference room. This session will cover the new priority level system and common documentation gaps we have been seeing. All staff are encouraged to attend, even if you have attended a similar training in the past.

Please let me know if you have any questions about the information in this memo.

**Memorandum**

**To:** All ARC Staff
**From:** Dana Whitfield, ARC Coordinator
**Date:** April 2, 2025
**Subject:** End-of-Year Reminders and Summer Planning

As we move into the final weeks of the spring semester, I want to take a moment to thank each of you for the work you have done this year. The volume of accommodation requests was higher than in any previous year, and the care you have shown students through finals week preparations has not gone unnoticed. This memo outlines the tasks we need to complete before the office closes for the summer, as well as some early thoughts about the fall.

**Equipment Returns**

Please remind any students who borrowed equipment from the ARC that all loaner items must be returned by **Friday, May 16, 2025**. This includes smartpens, digital recorders, FM systems, and ergonomic keyboards. Students who have approved summer accommodations may request an extension by emailing the office directly, but extensions will only be granted on a case-by-case basis and must be approved by me before May 9.

A full inventory of loaned equipment is attached to this memo. Please review it and flag any items you believe are missing or unaccounted for. We will conduct a physical inventory on **May 19 and 20**, so please do not schedule time off for those days unless you have already cleared it with me.

**Spring Semester Service Logs**

All service logs for the spring semester should be finalized in the database by **Friday, May 9**. I know that many of you have been busy with end-of-semester appointments, but it is important that we have accurate records before the summer break. Please review your entries for the months of January through April and make any necessary corrections. If you have not yet entered notes for appointments you held during the last two weeks of April, please do so as soon as possible.

For reference, the total number of accommodated exams we administered this spring was 1,847, up from 1,412 in the spring of 2024. This increase has placed a significant strain on our proctoring schedule, and I want to acknowledge the extra hours many of you have put in. We will be discussing proctoring capacity in the fall planning meetings.

**Summer Office Hours**

The ARC will maintain reduced office hours during the summer session, beginning **Monday, May 26**. Our hours will be **Monday through Thursday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM**, and we will be closed on Fridays. We will also be closed on Monday, May 26, in observance of Memorial Day.

During the summer, we will have a rotating on-call schedule for urgent accommodation requests. The schedule will be posted in the shared drive by May 20. If you have specific dates you will be unavailable during the summer, please add them to the shared calendar by **May 12** so that I can build the schedule accordingly.

**Fall 2025 Accommodation Letters**

Faculty will receive an email in early August with instructions for accessing fall accommodation letters through the faculty portal. As in past years, letters will be available no later than **August 15**, which gives faculty time to review them before the start of the semester. We encourage students to submit their accommodation requests by **July 1** to ensure that letters are ready on time, but we will continue to process requests received after that date on a rolling basis.

Please note that the university has adopted a new case management system that will go live on **August 1**. Training sessions for all ARC staff will be held during the week of July 21. Attendance is mandatory. More information about the training schedule will be sent out in June.

**Staff Appreciation Lunch**

We will hold our annual staff appreciation lunch on **Friday, May 16, from 12:00 to 14:00** in the ARC Conference Room. This is a casual event, and partners and family members are welcome to attend. Please RSVP to Maria by **May 9** so that we can provide an accurate count to the caterer. I want to take this opportunity to recognize the work of our graduate assistants, who have been instrumental in managing the front desk and supporting students throughout the year.
